newsitem.title: USA: PP&L says Susquehanna nuke running normally.
newsitem.headline: PP&L says Susquehanna nuke running normally.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power & Light said Tuesday that its decision to suspend work by an off-site contractor on a dry storage system for its Susquehanna nuclear plant has had no impact on the plant's operations.
"The delay in construction of the dry storage facility will have no impact on plant operations," the company said in a statement.

Vectra, based in San Jose, Calif., is the contractor building the dry storage system for keeping spent fuel at PP&L's Susquehanna facility, Herbert Woodeschick, a special assistant to the president for Susquehanna, told Reuters.
Vectra could not be reached immediately for comment.
The Susquehanna facility, located in Berwick, Pa., comprises two nuclear power units, each rated at 1,090 megawatts.
"We had some concerns about the quality of the concrete modules and the canisters," said Woodeschick.
Asked how long it likely would take to resolve the problem, he replied "I have no idea."
Woodeschick said PP&L originally expected to spend about $20 million on the storage facility, including some in-house work, at the time the plan was announced in December, 1994.
He declined to give a current estimate for the overall cost of the project.
